source: ACIAR AH/2005/086 'Smallholder Cattle Best Practice Manual' (Windsor, Bush & Young), Best Practice Health and Husbandry of Cattle, Cambodia -- hosted at mekonglivestock.wordpress.com (University of Sydney / GDAHP project site)
text: The manual describes the main cattle and buffalo types found in Cambodia. Local cattle ('gor srok') are small, early-maturing, generally quiet animals reaching 250-350kg at maturity, showing a small hump suggesting Bos indicus origin; they are common in rice-growing areas and well adapted to lower-energy diets. Haryana cattle and their crosses are larger Bos indicus animals (up to 500kg when well fed), better suited to draught but requiring more maintenance feed and less quiet-tempered than local cattle. Brahman crosses are increasingly common but have higher feed requirements, walk slowly, and can have poorer breeding ability, making them somewhat less well adapted to Cambodian smallholder conditions. Swamp buffalo weigh 350-600+kg at maturity, need access to shade and water for temperature regulation, and are suited to draught work in heavy, wet soils, but their numbers are decreasing partly due to low reproductive rates.
